remarks: Tubular slide stays. No ring in slide bow or bell bow. Tubular slide stays. Flat bell-stay, with sizeable protuberance on side closest to bell-bow, decoration showing angel playing a trombone, also floral-leaf-acorn pattern. Hinge with pin on bell-pipe side; eyelet on bell-pipe side. A small wire is attached to the bell stay; one end of the wire is attached to the head of the pin in the hinge, the other to the eyelet. The wire is draped around a sharp protruberance on the stay. The instrument has an associated case (#438a) bearing the coat of arms of Nuremberg and the date 1767. The instrument may have belonged to the Nuremberg Stadtpfeiferei. An alto shawm by J. C. Denner in the same collection (#436a) has a similar case, with the same coat of arms and date, and the owner’s stamp “S. Heckel / St. Musicus”.⁵
